item.title: Silent Mode
item.description:
Silent Mode #

Silent mode is configured in /config. Toggle Silent mode there.

By default, silent mode is off, and the bot asks for the save location of each file.

When silent mode is enabled, the bot saves files directly to the default location without confirmation. Set the default storage and directory in /config before enabling it.

item.title: Storage Rules
item.description:
Storage Rules #

Storage rules allow you to define redirection rules when the bot uploads files to storage, so that saved files are automatically organized.

See: #28

Send /rules to view the current mode and rules, enable or disable rule matching, and delete rules. Add rules and import presets with the commands below.

Currently supported rule types:

  1. FILENAME-REGEX
  2. MESSAGE-REGEX
  3. IS-ALBUM

Basic syntax for adding rules:

“RuleType RuleContent StorageID|StorageName Path”

A numeric storage argument is treated as a storage ID (shown on the Storages page of the web console); anything else is treated as a storage name. Use an ID when the name contains spaces, or quote the name. Below is an example of a valid rule command:

item.title: Watch Chats
item.description:
Watch Chats #

This feature requires enabling UserBot integration.

You can watch messages in a specific chat and automatically save them to the default storage, following storage rules. You can also add filters so that only matching messages are saved.

Send /watch to manage watched chats:

  • Add watch — shows the syntax for adding a chat
  • Watched chats — lists watched chats and lets you stop each one
  • Notifications — toggles task notifications for all watched chats
  • Sync peers — imports the Userbot dialog list into the peer cache

item.title: URL Downloads
item.description:
URL Downloads #

Use the /download command with one or more links and select an engine:

  • Direct — plain HTTP/HTTPS download, best for ordinary file links
  • Aria2 — when Aria2 is enabled, including magnet and torrent links
  • Video — when yt-dlp is available, for supported video sites
/download <url1> [url2] [url3] ...

Examples:

/download https://example.com/file.zip
/download https://example.com/file1.zip https://example.com/file2.zip

Choose the engine, then select the target storage. For video sites, yt-dlp options such as -f best or --extract-audio can be appended to the same command.

item.title: Aria2 Downloads
item.description:
Aria2 Downloads #

This feature requires enabling Aria2 under **Settings → Aria2** and configuring the RPC connection.

Aria2 downloads are available through /download. Send links, then choose Aria2. It supports HTTP/HTTPS, FTP, BitTorrent, and magnet links.

/download <uri1> [uri2] [uri3] ...

Examples:

# Download an HTTP link
/download https://example.com/file.zip

# Download a magnet link
/download magnet:?xt=urn:btih:...

# Download a torrent file
/download https://example.com/file.torrent

Choose Aria2, then select the target storage. When only Aria2 supports the supplied links, it is the only engine available.

item.title: Video Downloads (yt-dlp)
item.description:
Video Downloads (yt-dlp) #

This feature requires the yt-dlp command-line tool installed on your system.

Video extraction is available through /download. Send a supported video URL, then choose Video (yt-dlp). It supports YouTube, Bilibili, Twitter, and 1000+ other sites.

/download <url1> [url2] [flags...]

Examples:

# Basic download
/download https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ

# Download multiple videos
/download https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=video1 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=video2

# Use custom parameters
/download https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ -f best
/download https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ --extract-audio --audio-format mp3

item.title: Storage Transfer
item.description:
Storage Transfer #

Use the /transfer command to transfer files directly between different storages without going through Telegram.

/transfer <source_storage>:/<source_path> [filter]

Parameters:

  • source_storage: Source storage name
  • source_path: Source path
  • filter: Optional regex filter to transfer only matching files

Examples:

# Transfer entire directory
/transfer local1:/downloads

# Transfer files from specified path
/transfer alist1:/media/photos

# Transfer only mp4 files
/transfer webdav1:/videos ".*\.mp4$"

# Transfer image files
/transfer local1:/pictures "(?i)\.(jpg|png|gif)$"

item.title: Save Files Outside Telegram
item.description:
Save Files Outside Telegram #

Besides files on Telegram, the bot can also save files from other websites via JavaScript plugins or built-in parsers.

See the Contributing Parsers document for details.

Send a link that matches a parser. Built-in parsers:

  • Twitter
  • Kemono

JavaScript plugin API #

JavaScript plugins register one parser with:

registerParser({
 metadata: {
 name: 'example',
 version: '1.0.0',
 apiVersion: '1',
 description: 'Example plugin',
 author: 'you',
 },
 canHandle(url) { return url.includes('example.com') },
 parse(url) {
 return {
 site: 'example',
 url,
 title: 'Example',
 resources: [{ url: 'https://cdn.example.com/file.zip', filename: 'file.zip' }],
 }
 },
})

apiVersion is the plugin ABI version and is independent of the plugin’s own version. The current ABI is "1"; plugins with another value are rejected. The available globals are console, ghttp (get, getJSON, head), and playwright. parse returns an Item with resources containing url, filename, optional mime_type, extension, size, hash, headers, and extra.

item.title: File Naming & Conflict Strategies
item.description:
File Naming & Conflict Strategies #

SaveAny-Bot lets you customize how saved files are named and how collisions with existing files are resolved, directly in Telegram with /config and /template.

/config — User Settings #

The /config command contains the following per-user settings:

  • Filename strategy — how the saved file is named
  • Duplicate file strategy — what happens when a file with the same name already exists in the target storage
  • Silent mode — save incoming files directly to the default location
  • Default storage — choose the storage (and directory) used by silent mode and unmatched rules
  • Filename template — view the current template and the /template usage

Settings are stored per user and apply to all of that user’s subsequent save/transfer tasks.

item.title: HTTP API
item.description:
HTTP API #

SaveAny-Bot provides an HTTP API that allows you to programmatically create download/transfer tasks, query task status, cancel tasks, and more — without going through Telegram.

Enabling the API #

The API shares the web console listener and port; there is nothing separate to enable. The web console listens on 127.0.0.1:28080 by default. Set an access token under Settings → Web:

  • Access token: used for direct Web UI access through /?token=... and with Authorization: Bearer <token> for the API.
  • Web listen address: shared by the console and API; use 0.0.0.0:28080 when it must be reachable from other hosts.

All endpoints live under /api/v1.

item.title: CLI Subcommands
item.description:
CLI Subcommands #

Besides running the Telegram bot with ./saveany-bot (no subcommand), the binary exposes two helper subcommands for moving local files into a storage backend: upload (one-shot) and watch (continuous).

These subcommands load the same database settings as the bot, initialize the database and caches, then perform their task. They do not start the Telegram bot itself, although storages of type telegram will spin up the bot client just for the upload.
